page: Microsoft Azure D8ps_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on 64-bit ARM architecture, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on this instance type.

The D8ps_v7 instance includes no local ephemeral storage out of the box, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage capabilities for OS and data disk operations. Public network connectivity requires external allocation, as zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the instance. Because it utilizes the arm64 instruction set, workloads must be compiled for or compatible with the ARM software ecosystem.

By leveraging an ARM-based compute architecture, the D8ps_v7 provides resource-dense compute and memory allocations designed for cost-efficient operational profiles compared to traditional x86 alternatives. Tradeoffs include reliance on external attached storage for all I/O needs and lack of integrated x86 instruction extensions.

This server type is suitable for general-purpose enterprise tasks compatible with 64-bit ARM environments, such as multi-tier web applications, application servers, microservices architectures, continuous integration runners, and mid-sized containerized services.
